questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A study group revises full employment; which statement is correct?

options.text: Full employment means no cyclical unemployment.
Full employment means no frictional unemployment.
Full employment means everyone works full-time.

questions.explanation: Full employment occurs when cyclical unemployment is zero; frictional and structural remain. The tempting view demands zero unemployment. Natural rate remains.

questions.stem: Explain why the short-run Phillips curve shows an inverse inflation-unemployment tradeoff.

answer.exemplar: In the short run, higher demand raises both prices and employment, so lower unemployment accompanies higher inflation.

questions.explanation: Demand boosts raise output and prices together; the tempting view says the tradeoff is permanent. It is short-run only.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Explain why the expectations-augmented Phillips curve becomes vertical in the long run.

answer.exemplar: In the long run, expectations adjust, so unemployment returns to its natural rate at any inflation rate, making the curve vertical.

questions.explanation: Expectations adjust fully, restoring natural unemployment; the tempting view says policy can hold unemployment low. Long-run neutrality applies.
